name: Mobile Uploader
description: Secure file upload API for mobile applications using Jellyfin authentication with dynamic library access and folder management
overview: Upload files to Jellyfin libraries through a mobile-optimized REST API. Users authenticate with their Jellyfin accounts and can upload to any library they have access to. Features include automatic library discovery, folder browsing and creation, and comprehensive security validation.

versions.changelog: Release with Jellyfin user authentication, mobile-optimized API endpoints, and dynamic library management
Backend integration: license verification, payment-proof gate, IAP receipt validation, multi-device tracking, maintenance-mode awareness.
Adds in-dashboard configuration page: Backend URL, API key, security token (with regenerate), per-user license mapping summary, free-tier limits, allowed extensions. No more hand-editing XML on disk.

QR-code app setup + config UI hardening. Generate a QR from the plugin config page that the mobile app scans to fill server URL, API key, and security token in one tap. Also removes free-tier limits and premium-bypass toggles from the UI to prevent server admins from unlocking unpaid features.

Better network detection + locked-down backend config. New ClientApparentIP signal (the IP the inbound request comes from, as seen by the server) gives an authoritative same-LAN check with zero outbound calls. Local-IP enumeration rewritten to skip Docker, VPN, and virtual adapters. Backend connection settings (URL, verification endpoint, allowed package) removed from the dashboard — those values are deployment-locked and shouldn't be admin-editable.
AllowedAppPackage now accepts a comma-separated list so debug/beta build variants of the mobile app can authenticate against the same server without rotating the plugin config.

Multi-path library support across folder CRUD. Libraries mapped to more than one filesystem path (e.g. TV Shows pointing at /media/TV AND /external/TV) now surface subfolders from every location instead of just the first one returned by Jellyfin's virtual mount. Create / rename / delete were rewritten to resolve the right physical root before touching disk, so operations land next to their siblings even when they live under a non-primary path.
